Thanks for the productive call earlier 

quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned.

High-level success criteria (from our discussion):
- Latency: p95 generation latency <= 250ms for 512-token requests on your reserved instance profile.
- Quality: endpoint passes your eval set F1/accuracy baseline (we'll use the set Priya sent).
- Throughput: sustain 200 concurrent users with <=2s tail under expected traffic pattern.
- Security: data residency in us-west, server-to-server auth, and KMS-managed keys for any customer data persisted.

Evaluation plan / timeline:
- 30-day POC window starting after kickoff.
- Week 0: sandbox keys + sample SDK + integration smoke tests.
- Week 1-2: feature integration (streaming responses, tool-calling for retrieval), run evals against your dataset.
- Week 3: scale/perf testing and collect cost estimates.
- Week 4: stakeholder review and go/no-go.

Thanks 

Adding the implementation details from the SE side. Below is a concise integration plan and the API/SDK notes you'll need to get started. I attached a short code snippet file (sdk-integration-snippet.txt) with examples for Python/Node.

Integration summary (recommended):
- SDKs: official Redwood SDKs for Python and Node (pip/npm). We also have a thin HTTP client if you prefer direct REST.
- Auth: Server-to-server API keys (rotateable). For POC we can use scoped keys; for Private/Dedicated we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations (we'll open an enterprise request to enable CMK on your environment).
- Endpoints (REST):
  - POST /v1/generate  -> synchronous generation (JSON request/response)
  - POST /v1/stream    -> streaming generation (SSE with chunked JSON payloads)
  - POST /v1/embeddings -> embeddings for retrieval/semantic search
  - POST /v1/tool_call -> tool/function calling payloads (if using function-calling pattern)

Streaming notes:
- We surface streaming via Server-Sent Events (SSE) + chunked JSON; SDKs provide a helpers/stream() method that yields partial tokens. Websocket option available for low-latency bidirectional flows but SSE is simpler to integrate into service-side pipelines.

Tool calling / retrieval pattern:
- We support the function-calling pattern (JSON schema-driven) where you declare tool interfaces and the model returns a structured call. Alternatively, you can implement a 2-step retrieval flow (embeddings -> candidate ranking -> generation with retrieval context). Both are supported with examples in the attached snippet.

Performance hints (for POC profile):
- Use prefix/KV caching for repeated prompt prefixes (we can provision a shared cache for your tests).
- For 512-token workloads, we recommend batch sizes of 8-16 for throughput testing; keep single-request latency tests as uncached single-shot calls.
- We can enable quantized variants on Dedicated if you want to test cost/latency tradeoffs.

Suggested POC resourcing & timeline:
- Redwood SE time: 2 full-day onboarding + 4 x 2hr office-hours sessions across the first 2 weeks.
- Expect 1-2 Acme engineers for 1-2 weeks to wire SDK calls and run smoke tests.

Next steps I can action now:
- Share a sandbox API key and the sample repo (I'll post links).
- Set up a 60-minute technical kickoff on 30 Mar 10:00 PT (calendar invite to follow).
- Open an internal ticket to request CMK enablement for your account (Priya, I'll need the KMS key id once we confirm).
